walkthroughs.body_html:
Independent Investigation (NEA) — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Independent Investigation (NEA) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Independent Investigation (NEA).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What was the Tohoku earthquake magnitude?

options: Qualitative data means high-quality data and quantitative means a lot of data.
A drainage basin is the bowl-shaped area at the mouth of the river.
The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries, bounded by a watershed (high ground that separates one basin from another).
A drainage basin is the underground source of a river.

mcqs.q: What is lag time on a storm hydrograph?
options: Qualitative data means high-quality data and quantitative means a lot of data.
Lag time is how long the storm itself lasts.
The time between peak rainfall and peak river discharge — affected by drainage basin shape, land use, soil saturation and vegetation.
Lag time is the delay between thunder and lightning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between qualitative and quantitative data?
options: Quantitative data is always more scientific and reliable than qualitative.
A drainage basin is the underground source of a river.
Qualitative data means high-quality data and quantitative means a lot of data.
Quantitative data is numerical and measurable (traffic counts, river width); qualitative data is descriptive and non-numerical (interview quotes, photo descriptions, field sketches).
